diagnostic_evidence.quote: For a fixed number of basis functions $N \ge 3$, the Lebesgue constant $\Lambda_N$ for interpolation in the basis $\{w_j(x)\}$ is unbounded as the extension parameter $\delta \to \infty$.

issues.failure_explanation: The Lebesgue constant is the norm of the interpolation operator into the space span{w_j} restricted to I; it does not depend on the conditioning of any particular basis representation. Writing s = pi(x-L/2)/(L+2 delta) in [-tau, tau] with tau -> 0 as delta -> infinity, the functions sin(j pi/2 + j s) have Taylor coefficients in s whose degree-(0..N-1) matrix is invertible (parity-split generalized Vandermonde in j^2), so the rescaled space converges to the polynomials of degree <= N-1 in u = s/tau on [-1,1], and interpolation at the fixed relative nodes converges to polynomial interpolation there. Hence Lambda_N(delta) tends to the finite Lebesgue constant of polynomial interpolation (for N=2 one computes Lambda_2 -> 1), so it is bounded as delta -> infinity and the theorem is false. The proof's inference is invalid: the blow-up of ||W^{-1}|| in the normalized eigenbasis is exactly compensated by the collapse of the basis functions on I (near-null coefficient vectors produce uniformly small functions on I), so sigma_min(W) -> 0 implies nothing about Lambda_N.

failure_location.quote: The Lebesgue constant, which depends on the norm of the inverse of the collocation matrix, must therefore be unbounded as $\delta \to \infty$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the statement with what the argument actually shows: the scaled collocation matrix converges to a singular matrix, so the coefficient system becomes arbitrarily ill-conditioned as delta -> infinity, while the Lebesgue constant stays bounded and converges to the polynomial-interpolation Lebesgue constant at the fixed relative nodes; delete the ill-posedness and optimal-delta conclusions.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem and the following remark ('the interpolation problem becomes ill-posed', 'there is an optimal, problem-dependent value of delta') are false within the paper's own Lebesgue-constant framework: for fixed N the basis interpolation remains stable as the extension grows.
issues.title: False claim that the basis-interpolation Lebesgue constant is unbounded as delta -> infinity
issues.why_classification: The stated claim is false and the truth is essentially the opposite (bounded, convergent Lambda_N); no comparable Lebesgue-constant instability survives, so the substantive result is abandoned and only a different-type matrix-conditioning statement remains, changing the guarantee type.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since our basis functions are eigenfunctions of the Laplacian on the extended domain, this new basis is explicitly $\{\phi_j(x) = \lambda_j w_j(x)\}$.
By definition, for any function $f(x)$ that is already in the interpolation space $\Phi_N$, its interpolant is itself, i.e., $\mathcal{I}_N f = f$.
The Lebesgue constant for the Poisson operator shows super-polynomial growth, while the Lebesgue constant for the convection-diffusion operator shows obviously much slower growth.

issues.failure_explanation: Because phi_j = -w_j'' = lambda_j w_j with lambda_j > 0, span{phi_j}_{j<=N} = span{w_j}_{j<=N} = V_N: scaling each basis function by its eigenvalue does not alter the interpolation space. The Lebesgue constant of the paper's own definition depends only on the interpolation space and the collocation nodes, so the Lebesgue constant for the Poisson right-hand-side interpolation is identical to the basis-interpolation constant, which Theorem thm:basis_bound proves is O(cot(pi delta/(L+2 delta)) log N) on the same uniform grids. The claim of super-polynomial growth therefore contradicts the paper's own Theorem thm:basis_bound and is false. The proof's Step 1 is also a non-sequitur: for f in the interpolation space the operator-norm ratio is ||I_N f||/||f|| = 1, not ||f||_infty / max_k |f(x_k)| (that bound requires different data g with the same nodal values but small sup norm); and the same Step 1 applied to f = w_N in V_N would 'prove' the basis interpolation unstable, again contradicting Theorem thm:basis_bound.

failure_location.quote: The associated Lebesgue constant, $\Lambda_N$, is not bounded by any polynomial in $N$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the theorem with the statement that Phi_N = V_N and hence Lambda_N = O(cot(pi delta/(L+2 delta)) log N) by Theorem thm:basis_bound; remove the dichotomy claims throughout and correct Section 8 (matrix conditioning is not the Lebesgue constant).
issues.overall_effect: The paper's first key result and the advertised stability dichotomy collapse: the Poisson collocation right-hand-side interpolation is in fact logarithmically stable. The abstract/intro instability claims, the Stability Dichotomy remark, the d-dimensional Poisson-instability remark in Section 7 (where span{lambda_j w_j} = span{w_j} as well), and the Section 8 narrative/caption (a condition number of a column-scaled matrix is presented as the Lebesgue constant of the Poisson operator) all become unreliable.
issues.title: Poisson super-polynomial growth claim is false: the operator does not change the interpolation space
issues.why_classification: No comparable version of the instability claim survives: the correct statement is the opposite (logarithmic stability), the headline dichotomy is abandoned, and the dependent prose and numerical framing must be rewritten.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: A careful but lengthy algebraic reduction shows that the expression $\frac{2q_j^3 + 2kp_jq_j + q_j^2 + kp_j}{2q_j^2(\alpha+1)}$ is very close to $m_k$.
The total error $\Delta_k = \frac{\theta_k(N)}{\pi} - m_k$ can be shown to be bounded by:

issues.failure_explanation: The statement is false for all L, delta > 0. The angles theta_k(N) = theta_0 + k Delta_N have spacing Delta_N = N pi L/((N-1)(L+2 delta)) < pi once N > 1 + L/(2 delta) and total range N pi L/(L+2 delta) >= pi once N >= (L+2 delta)/L; the grid therefore forms a Delta_N-net over more than a full period of sine, so max_k |sin theta_k(N)| >= cos(Delta_N/2) >= cos(pi L/(L+2 delta)) > 0 for all sufficiently large N, and no subsequence can yield decay, let alone exponential decay. The appendix proof is invalid: it asserts without proof ('a careful but lengthy algebraic reduction') that theta_k(N)/pi lies within C q_j |alpha - p_j/q_j| of the integer m_k = k p_j + q_j. Already at k = 0 the difference is theta_0/pi - q_j = (1 - 2 q_j alpha)/(2(alpha+1)) approximately (1 - 2 p_j)/(2(alpha+1)), which is generically far from any integer (e.g. for the convergent 7/5 of sqrt(2) it is about -2.69), so the claimed O(1/q_{j+1}) error bound fails and the construction cannot make all theta_k close to multiples of pi.

failure_location.quote:
There exist an infinite subsequence of integers $\{N_j\}_{j=1}^\infty$ and a constant $c > 0$ (depending on $L$ and $\delta$) such that
\[
\max_{k \in \{0, \dots, N_j-1\}} |\sin(\theta_k(N_j))| < e^{-cN_j}
\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the lemma and its appendix proof; the true statement is max_k |sin theta_k(N)| >= cos(pi L/(L+2 delta)) > 0 for all N > max(1 + L/(2 delta), (L+2 delta)/L), which yields no super-polynomial lower bound on Lambda_N.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:added-2 loses the only ingredient of its Step 2 (independently of that theorem's own fatal basis-independence flaw); the claimed Runge-type super-polynomial instability is unestablished, and the correct statement is a uniform positive lower bound on the discrete maximum.
issues.title: KeyLemma on exponential avoidance of sine peaks by the uniform grid is false; appendix proof invalid
issues.why_classification: The statement is false (the opposite uniform lower bound holds) and its proof rests on an unsupported and incorrect assertion; the result must be abandoned, and with it falls its linchpin role in the paper's first main theorem.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: A careful analysis shows that for nodes in $[a,b] \subset (0,L)$ and evaluation points $x \in (-\delta, 0)$, the integral is bounded by $C/K$ for a constant $C$ that depends on the geometry ($L, \delta, a, b$) but not on the degree $M$.
The left-hand side of this inequality is crucial: it shows that the continuous norm on $I$ is controlled by the values of $g$ at these $K$ discrete points.
Let the operator be $L[u] = -u_{xx} + k_0 u_x$ for a non-zero constant $k_0$.

issues.failure_explanation: No degree-independent constant C_R exists: a degree-M trigonometric polynomial can concentrate its L^2 mass in the extension strip. The Fejer kernel of degree M centered at x_0 = -delta/2 in the strip has ||F_M||^2_{L^2(tilde I)} of order M while its L^2 mass on I is O(M^{-2}) (tails bounded by 1/(M t^2) beyond distance delta/2), so the ratio ||g||_{L^2(tilde I)}/||g||_{L^2(I)} is unbounded as M grows (bandlimited-concentration/Slepian constructions give exponential growth). The appendix proof's pivotal estimate int_{J_1} sum_j |ell_j(x)|^2 dx <= C_geom/K is false: trigonometric Lagrange functions for nodes in [a,b] grow exponentially in M at extrapolation points x in (-delta,0), so the integral grows with M rather than decaying like 1/K; and the Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund equivalence invoked at the start (samples in [L/4,3L/4] controlling the L^2(I) norm with M-independent constants) is itself the same false nested-interval claim. The lemma is the middle link of the stability chain in Theorems thm:convdiff, thm:added-3, thm:added-5, so those proofs collapse. Internal check: the proof of Theorem thm:convdiff never uses k_0 nonzero, so if the chain were valid it would prove the Poisson Lebesgue constant polynomially bounded, contradicting Theorem thm:added-2.

failure_location.quote:
Then there exists a constant $C_R$, which depends only on the geometry of $I$ and $\tilde{I}$ but is independent of the polynomial degree $M$, such that for any $g \in P_M$:
\[
\norm{g}_{L^2(\tilde{I})} \le C_R \norm{g}_{L^2(I)}.
\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace this lemma with a valid stability link between ||L[u_N]||_{L^2(tilde I)} and the discrete samples (e.g., a direct analysis of the collocation matrix, or an oversampled least-squares formulation with a frame inequality), because the degree-independent Remez inequality is false and the present chain cannot yield a polynomial bound.
issues.overall_effect: The central polynomial-stability theorem for convection-diffusion and its variable-coefficient and multidimensional extensions lose their proofs. Since any correct Remez constant grows with the degree, the same strategy yields at best an exponentially growing bound on ||A^{-1}|| and Lambda_N, so the advertised polynomial bound (and the abstract's 'provably polynomial' claim) is unestablished.
issues.title: Degree-independent Remez-type norm equivalence is false; appendix proof's key estimate is false
issues.why_classification: The lemma is false with an optimal constant that grows with the degree, so the central result's proof strategy delivers at best exponential bounds; no source-supported repair preserves the polynomial guarantee, which requires essentially new proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: A rigorous proof for collocation grids can be found, for example, in \cite{canuto2007spectral}.

issues.failure_explanation: As written, T_N ranges over all trigonometric polynomials of degree at most N, a space of dimension 2N+1 > N, so there exists a nonzero such T_N vanishing at all N grid points; then the left-hand side is 0 while ||T_N||_{L^2(I)} > 0, falsifying the inequality. The intended reading (T_N restricted to the N-dimensional space {L[u_N]}) is essential to the proofs of Theorems thm:convdiff, thm:added-3, thm:added-5 but is left unproved; the cited reference treats Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund inequalities for Gauss-type quadrature grids with matched weights, not uniform subinterval sampling of these Fourier-extension-type spaces with an N-independent constant. The only related bound the paper itself supports is c_1' >= c (log N)^{-2} for the sine space V_N, obtained from Theorem thm:basis_bound's Lebesgue-constant bound, not an N-independent constant.

failure_location.quote:
there exists a constant $c_1' > 0$ independent of $N$ such that:
\[
\sum_{i=1}^{N} |T_N(x_i)|^2 \ge c_1' \norm{T_N}_{L^2(I)}^2.
\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the statement to the N-dimensional range space {L[u_N]} and prove a discrete sampling inequality for it (e.g., from a Lebesgue-constant bound for that space), accepting a logarithmic or algebraic loss in c_1' that still yields a polynomial-type final bound on Lambda_N.
issues.overall_effect: The first link of the discrete-stability chain, ||A v||_2 >= C' ||L[u_N]||_{L^2(I)}, is unestablished, so the uniform lower bound on sigma_min(A) used to control ||A^{-1}|| and hence Lambda_N is unproved (independently of the false norm-equivalence lemma).
issues.title: Discrete sampling (Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund) inequality is false as stated and unproved for the required space
issues.why_classification: The false literal statement needs only a scope restriction, and the missing inequality for the intended space is a contained new lemma; a weakened (e.g. polylogarithmic) constant leaves a recognizably comparable polynomial-stability guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $P_M$ be the space of trigonometric polynomials of degree at most $M$.
Let the convection coefficient $k(x) \in C^1(I)$ satisfy the coercivity condition

issues.failure_explanation: For a variable coefficient, L[u_N] = sum_j c_j (lambda_j w_j + k(x) w_j') is not a trigonometric polynomial: with arbitrary k in C^1, the products k(x) w_j'(x) are generally not trigonometric. Lemmas lem:norm_equivalence and lem:mz_inequality are stated only for trigonometric polynomials, so neither applies to g = L[u_N]; that the constants would be independent of k(x) does not address the lemmas' hypotheses. Step 2 of the proof therefore uses its ingredients outside their scope, independently of the fact that those lemmas are themselves false (separate issues).

failure_location.quote: It relies on the norm-equivalence results of Lemma~\ref{lem:norm_equivalence} and Lemma~\ref{lem:mz_inequality}, which are independent of $k(x)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict k to be a fixed trigonometric polynomial (then L[u_N] is a trigonometric polynomial of degree O(N) and the lemmas apply), or prove Remez and sampling inequalities for the weighted space {L[u] : u in V_N}; the first option is a limited weakening preserving a comparable result.
issues.overall_effect: The polynomial-stability claim for slowly varying convection fields, and its d-dimensional version Theorem thm:added-5 (where k(x) multiplies the gradient), remain unproved even if the one-dimensional norm-equivalence lemmas are repaired.
issues.title: Variable-coefficient stability proof applies trigonometric-polynomial lemmas outside their hypotheses
issues.why_classification: A contained scope restriction (trigonometric-polynomial coefficients) or a contained new lemma for the weighted space repairs the step while leaving a recognizably comparable variable-coefficient stability statement.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The stated convergence rate then follows from the fundamental approximation properties of spectral methods for functions of finite Sobolev regularity.

issues.failure_explanation: Elliptic regularity gives u in H^{r+2}(I), but the error of the collocation solution u_N does not follow from regularity alone. One needs (i) a best-approximation rate for H^{r+2} functions in the extended-domain basis on I (nontrivial Fourier-extension approximation theory, since the basis functions vanish on the boundary of the extended domain, not of I), and (ii) a quasi-optimality/stability bound ||u - u_N|| <= (1 + Lambda_N) E_N(u). The paper's own stability bounds do not yield the stated rate: Theorem thm:convdiff's Lambda_N = O(N^{3.5}) would give only O(N^{3.5-(r+2)}), and Theorem thm:added-2's claimed super-polynomial Lambda_N would give no algebraic rate at all. The asserted O(N^{-(r+2)}) bound is therefore unsupported by, and in tension with, the paper's formal content.

failure_location.quote:
Consequently, the $L^2$-error of the spectral approximation is bounded by:
\[
\norm{u - u_N}_{L^2(I)} = O(N^{-(r+2)}).
\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert a quasi-optimality argument combining a valid Lebesgue-constant bound with a best-approximation rate in the extension basis; with the paper's stated Lambda_N = O(N^{3.5}) this yields a weakened rate or requires r large enough, while the stated rate is recovered only up to logarithmic factors if the corrected O(log N) stability is used.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence-rate guarantee of Section 6, and its d-dimensional restatement in Section 7, are unestablished; the claimed scope of problems achieving the stated algebraic convergence rates is unreliable.
issues.title: Convergence-rate theorem asserts a collocation error bound with no stability or quasi-optimality argument
issues.why_classification: The regularity conclusion stands and the rate claim is repairable by a contained but nontrivial quasi-optimality and approximation argument, at the cost of at most a limited weakening (logarithmic factors or a restriction on r).
